paragraphs: Decision center: the work of driver/sales workers is to turn these front-end conditions — delivery slips, orders, and routes, goods, payments, and documents, and vehicles, equipment, roads, and weather — into a route work chain that delivers on time, allows goods and payments to be reconciled, and holds driving and food safety boundaries: first verify the delivery slips, orders, routes, and goods and inspect the vehicle and equipment, then drive and deliver along the route and take orders and introduce new products and price changes at the delivery point, then collect payment and give change and issue receipts or charge to the account per the order, then stock shelves and set up promotions or restock vending machines and remove old goods, and finally record sales and delivery information, settle and reconcile, and maintain the vehicle and equipment and report anomalies. The point of judgment is not 'can the vehicle get there' but whether every step of the chain — loading, driving, delivery and sales, payment collection, stocking, and records and settlement — is accurate, reconcilable, and handled according to traffic, food safety, and payment rules.

Suitable for a first try: willing to drive outdoors and on the road for long periods and deal with all kinds of customers; able to work according to routes, delivery slips, and payment rules and stay careful about goods and payments and quantities; able to withstand weather and heat and cold and time pressure and repetitive handling; willing to do vehicle and equipment checks and cleaning and record keeping and to accept early starts and shifts and peak season rhythms.

Needs caution: if you expect this job to be sitting in the vehicle without any handling or reconciliation, or you are unwilling to follow traffic rules and driving safety and food safety and payment and receipt requirements (speeding and fatigued driving, writing slips casually without receipts, not counting goods and payments, treating vehicle and food equipment maintenance as optional), or you find it hard to stay patient and accurate when interacting with unpleasant or angry customers under time pressure, then the actual work experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk verification: using the fictional delivery slips, orders, route sheets, payment documents, and vehicle inspection sheet provided on this page, complete a paper exercise that 'arranges the loading and delivery sequence according to the delivery slips and route — writes a paragraph on delivery and payment collection and discrepancies according to the delivery and payment rules — and fills in one sales and delivery record and vehicle and equipment inspection and anomaly record', only to verify whether you are willing to check item by item according to the route and documents and rules and to record truthfully. The exercise uses fictional materials and does not involve real vehicles, roads, goods, or payments, and it does not constitute a conclusion on traffic violations or liability, food safety, product quality, or price compliance, nor is it equivalent to job training or an occupational qualification.

Decision center: whether delivery slips, orders, routes, payments, and vehicle status can be turned into a delivery, sales, and settlement chain that the fleet, store, and finance can all take up and verify.

The work is mainly outdoors and on the road and at customer sites with frequent customer interaction: outdoor exposure to all kinds of weather 'every day' 100%, time pressure every day 92%, exposure to extreme heat or extreme cold every day 82% (another 18% weekly or more), repeating the same tasks 'extremely important' 76% (another 18% important), continuous use of hands 76% (another 14% about half the time), inside an enclosed vehicle every day 78% (another 22% never), face-to-face discussions every day 77% (another 18% weekly or more); decision freedom 'very large' 43% (another 14% some, 14% no freedom), decisions every day 39% (another 14% weekly or more, 14% never), having to deal with unpleasant or angry people every day 19% (another 18% weekly or more), conflict situations 'weekly or more' 26% (another 15% yearly or more, 17% never); work hours 'regular' 82% (another 18% irregular), continuous repetitive motions 64% (another 17% more than half), continuous bending or twisting 59%, sitting 'more than half' 28%, exposure to contaminants every day 40%, competition 'extremely competitive' 21%, consequences of error 'extremely serious' 32% (another 19% serious, 12% not serious at all), working more than 40 hours per week 81%. The workplace is roads and the vehicle cab and customer delivery points and stores or warehouses, and the pace is determined by the route and delivery timeliness and customer demand and the season.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: this page is O*NET-SOC 53-3031.00 Driver/Sales Workers. Adjacent positions have different duties — heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers handle long-haul freight; light truck drivers focus on pure delivery without sales or payment collection; couriers and messengers focus on pickup and delivery of items and timeliness; retail salespersons close sales inside stores; cashiers settle payments at the checkout counter; stockers and order fillers organize and pick goods in warehouses and stores; industrial truck operators drive forklifts and tractors on site. This occupation is set on driving a vehicle along a set route or within a set area, delivering while selling or collecting payment and taking orders and stocking at delivery points. Traffic and occupational qualification and food safety and product and price requirements are governed by the regulations and competent authorities of the relevant jurisdiction and by this enterprise's systems, are not inferred from the job title, and must not exceed authorization to issue conclusions on traffic violations or liability, food safety, or compliance.

Inputs that must be verified: delivery slips and orders and route sheets and customer lists, goods and cargo and quantities and batch numbers and shelf life, price and promotion and payment and document and account-charging rules, vehicle and food dispensing equipment and refrigeration and safety status, road and weather and timeliness requirements, payment and discrepancy and return and rejection handling rules, and sales and delivery and settlement record requirements. Things that must not be done: departing without verifying the route and goods, speeding or driving while fatigued or distracted by using a phone, delivering unclean or expired goods, collecting payment without a receipt or changing prices on your own or omitting payment from the records, working with defective vehicles and equipment, concealing or delaying reports of discrepancies and damage and complaints, and promising prices or compensation or making liability determinations externally beyond authorization.

The fit judgment should be made by combining whether you can drive for long periods outdoors and on the road under time pressure, whether you can work according to routes and documents and payment rules and stay careful about payments and quantities, whether you can withstand weather and heat and cold and repetitive handling, whether you can do vehicle and equipment inspection and cleaning and record keeping, and whether you are clear about your duties and authorization and traffic and food safety and payment boundaries; it is not replaced by a self-assessment of 'being able to drive' or 'being able to run around'; all of this must be confirmed in supervised actual routes and shift lead observation.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real driving and delivery and sales and payment collection and food safety must be undertaken by organizations and personnel with the corresponding training and qualifications that follow the regulations of the relevant jurisdiction and this enterprise's systems; individuals must not exceed authorization to issue conclusions on traffic violations and liability, food safety, product quality, or price compliance externally, and this page does not constitute traffic, road transport, food safety, product quality, price, or legal advice.

The work object is sales or delivery on a set route or in a set area and may include food, medical supplies, newspapers, or commercial laundry. The six O*NET Core items include driving to deliver, introducing products and prices to regular customers, daily sales or delivery records, complaints, payment receipts, and vehicle and food equipment maintenance and cleaning; taking orders and collecting payment may be undertaken by definition and not every worker performs all tasks. Promotional displays, vending machine restocking, order contracts, checklist loading, and specialty food sales are Supplemental. Cold chain batch numbers and shelf life apply only to the goods actually applicable, and sign-off, reconciliation, and anomaly handover are editorial verification items for specific positions rather than uniform core outputs.

Judgment one: whether the delivery slips and route and goods are verified clearly — counting the load against the customer list and quantities and batch numbers and shelf life rather than loading from impression.

Judgment two: whether the vehicle and food and safety equipment are operable — inspecting the vehicle and refrigeration and food dispensing equipment and safety devices and clearing defects rather than driving out with problems.

Judgment three: whether driving and roads and timeliness are held — driving according to traffic rules and the route and timeliness and avoiding distraction and fatigue rather than breaking the rules to save time.

Judgment four: whether delivery and sales and stocking are standardized — completing delivery and order taking and introducing new products and price changes and stocking and promotional display according to the delivery point's needs rather than delivering arbitrarily.

Judgment five: whether payment collection and receipts and discrepancies are accurate — collecting payment and giving change and issuing receipts according to the price and payment rules and handling discrepancies and returns and rejections per the rules rather than leaving no receipt or omitting payment from the records.

Judgment six: whether records and settlement and anomalies are held — completing sales and delivery records and settlement reconciliation and vehicle and equipment maintenance and reporting and handing over per the system when damage or complaints or accidents or equipment anomalies occur, rather than concealing or delaying.

The work of driver/sales workers can be divided into three connected but independent work surfaces. The first is loading and route preparation: verify the delivery slips and orders and customer list and route sheet, count and load goods and cargo by quantity and batch number and shelf life, inspect the vehicle and refrigeration and food dispensing equipment and safety devices and replenish documents and promotional materials and payment float, and confirm the payment and account-charging and return and rejection rules. The second is driving and delivery and sales: drive the vehicle along the set route or within the set area, deliver goods at the delivery point and obtain the customer's sign-off, take orders and introduce new products and price changes, stock shelves and set up promotional displays or hand out promotional materials, collect payment and restock and remove stale goods for vending machines, collect payment and give change and issue receipts or charge to the account per the order, listen to and handle customer complaints about goods or services, and when necessary collect items such as commercial laundry or hand them to the customer. The third is records and settlement and vehicle maintenance: record sales and delivery information on the daily sales or delivery record, complete payment and document settlement and reconciliation and handle discrepancies and returns and rejections, maintain the vehicle and food dispensing equipment and clean the interior of food or beverage dispensers, and inspect vehicle and equipment status and report per the requirements and complete handover when damage or complaints or accidents or equipment anomalies occur. All three work surfaces proceed within the delivery slips, route, price and payment rules, and traffic and food safety requirements.

Where are the boundaries between driver/sales workers and heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers, light truck drivers, couriers and messengers, retail salespersons, cashiers, and stockers and order fillers?

This page's 53-3031 sells or delivers along a route/area, and payment collection and order taking may be tasks; heavy 53-3032 is towing trailers or trucks with a gross weight of at least 26001 pounds including trailers and requires a CDL, but is not entirely equivalent to long haul; light 53-3033 is under 26001 pounds, mainly picks up and delivers goods and may load and unload, but it is not asserted that payment collection never occurs. Couriers 43-5021 may deliver items on foot, by bicycle, or by public transport, and retail 41-2031 consumer goods sales are not limited to indoor stores; cashiers 41-2011 handle receipts and payments for non-financial institutions, and order fillers 53-7065 handle warehouse/yard/shelf orders. Qualifications are not mutually recognized by name.
Core purpose

Turn delivery slips, orders, routes, payments, and vehicle status into a route sales result that is delivered on time and can be reconciled: routes and goods clear, vehicle and equipment operable, driving and timeliness compliant, delivery and sales standardized, and payment collection and records accurate.

Editorial adjacent task comparison: heavy tractor-trailer freight is verified by vehicle type and weight and transport task and is not limited to long-haul trunk lines; light delivery focuses on pickup and delivery and may collect payment; couriers may travel on foot, by bicycle, or by other transport; retail sells goods to consumers and is not limited to stores, cashiers handle payments, and stocking and order filling focus on inventory orders, so duties may overlap.
Main objects and basis

The objects are delivery slips and orders and route sheets and customer lists, goods and cargo and quantities and batch numbers and shelf life, price and promotion and payment and document and account-charging rules, vehicle and food dispensing equipment and refrigeration and safety status, road and weather and timeliness requirements, and sales and delivery and settlement records; the basis is the delivery slips and route and price and payment rules and traffic and food safety requirements.

Objects and basis of adjacent positions: trunk goods and trailers and transport contracts (freight transport procedures); delivery items and routes (delivery procedures); express items and waybills and timeliness (express service specifications); store goods and displays and customers (retail operating specifications); checkout counter and payment and documents (cashier procedures); inventory and locations and orders (warehousing and order filling procedures).
Core process

Loading and route preparation → driving and delivery and sales → delivery and payment collection and invoicing → stocking and promotional display → records and settlement and vehicle and equipment maintenance and anomaly reporting.

Editorial task gaps: heavy vehicle driving and loading and unloading and trailer tasks are not limited to long haul; light pickup and delivery may collect payment; courier pickup and delivery may not involve driving; retail explains and recommends goods to consumers and is not limited to stores; cashier payment and change and records, and order filling inventory verification, are verified against the actual position, and the flows are not the single sequence of every occupation.
Main outputs

Delivery and sales records completed by route and timeliness, delivery and sign-off and stocking and display records, payment and invoicing and account-charging and discrepancy handling records, vehicle and equipment inspection and cleaning and maintenance records, and damage and complaint and accident and equipment anomaly reporting and handover records.

Outputs of adjacent positions: waybills and transport and delivery records; delivery and sign-off records; pickup and delivery item and timeliness records; sales and membership and inventory records; cashier and reconciliation and discrepancy records; inventory and order filling and verification records.
Responsible parties

This occupation bears execution responsibility for completing delivery and sales and payment collection and records according to the delivery slips and route and price and payment rules; responsibility for traffic violations and accidents and food safety and product quality and price compliance is borne by the driver together with the organization and the competent authorities according to regulations and systems.

Responsibilities of adjacent positions: long-haul transport is borne by the driver and the carrier; light delivery is borne by the driver and the organization; express delivery is borne by the courier and the express company; store retail is borne by the salesperson and the store; cashiering is borne by the cashier and the store; stocking and order filling are borne by the stocker and the store or warehouse.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with dispatch and the warehouse and the store and finance and customers, and adjust priorities according to the route and timeliness and customer and season; immediately report traffic accidents and damage and payment discrepancies and complaints and equipment anomalies and matters beyond authorization.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: long-haul freight interfaces with dispatch and loading and unloading and the receiving party; light delivery interfaces with the warehouse and the receiving party; express delivery interfaces with the branch and sorting and the recipient; store retail interfaces with the stockroom and the checkout and customers; cashiering interfaces with the front desk and finance; stocking and order filling interface with the stockroom and the front desk and delivery.
Conclusion boundaries

Do not depart without verifying the route and goods, do not speed or drive while fatigued or distracted by using a phone, do not deliver unclean or expired goods, do not collect payment without a receipt or change prices on your own or omit payment from the records, do not work with defective vehicles and equipment, do not conceal or delay reports of discrepancies and damage and complaints, do not promise prices or compensation or make liability determinations externally beyond authorization, and do not issue conclusions on traffic violations or liability, food safety, or compliance externally beyond authorization.

The boundaries of adjacent positions are determined by their respective traffic and transport and food safety and price systems and the regulations of the relevant jurisdiction; similar job titles do not mean the duties are interchangeable.
In this job, which judgments are most prone to error, and how should they be verified?

Common errors cluster in four areas: first, departing without verifying the delivery slips and route and goods clearly, resulting in wrong or missed deliveries and quantities, batch numbers, and shelf life not matching; second, failing to check vehicle and equipment and safety status, resulting in breakdowns on the road and spoiled goods and personal risk; third, breaking rules or being distracted under driving and timeliness pressure, resulting in traffic violations and accidents; fourth, non-standard delivery and payment collection and record keeping, resulting in goods and payments not matching and inability to reconcile and complaints. The verification method is that each item has a basis that can be looked back on: the loading and route and customer and quantity checklist, vehicle and equipment inspection and defect removal records, delivery and sign-off and stocking and display records, and payment and invoicing and account-charging and discrepancy handling records and reporting and handover records, rather than memory or verbal understanding.

Article 29 provides that the qualification certificate is valid for 6 years and renewal is required no later than 30 days before expiry, and Article 32 provides for cancellation for exceeding 63 and other reasons. Road Traffic Safety Law 2021: Article 19 requires the corresponding driving license and permitted vehicle type; Article 21 requires a careful inspection of safety and technical performance before departure and prohibits driving a vehicle with safety hazards; Article 22 prohibits driving under conditions such as excessive fatigue that affect safe driving. Article 70 requires stopping immediately at an accident to protect the scene, immediately rescuing the injured and promptly calling the police; where there is no injury and no dispute over the facts and cause, the parties may immediately leave the scene and restore traffic and negotiate, and if they do not leave they must promptly call the police, while for minor property damage with clear facts they should leave first and then negotiate. Article 73 provides that the public security traffic management department prepares the accident determination letter, and the individual or organization does not issue a formal liability conclusion on its own. General complaints and payment discrepancies and accidents cannot be handled by the same stop-work and reporting sequence; enterprise restart systems were not obtained. Food Safety Law 2025 revision government text: Article 33, item 6, covers safe, harmless, and clean containers, tools, and equipment for transport, storage, and loading and unloading, pollution prevention, the required temperature and humidity conditions, and not transporting together with toxic or harmful items; this item also applies to non-food operators engaged in storage, transport, and loading and unloading. Article 45 covers the health system and the annual health examination certificate for personnel who come into contact with directly edible food, and it is not a uniform health certificate for all packaged food delivery workers. Article 44 covers training and management of operating enterprises and the responsibility of the principal person in charge; Article 47 provides that if operating conditions no longer meet requirements rectification is required, and that if there is a potential food accident risk food operations must be stopped immediately and reported to the food safety department at or above the county level where the business is located; Article 63 provides that food that does not meet standards or may be harmful is stopped, notified, and recalled according to law by the corresponding producer or operator, and it is not an authority for delivery workers to destroy it at will. Article 41 additionally provides for a permitted transport system for road bulk transport of key liquid foods, which covers only that specific scope, and the specific catalog and supporting rules were not verified this round and are not generalized to ordinary parcels.
Are sales and delivery records and settlement reconciliation and vehicle and equipment maintenance completed and verifiable by shift, and do goods and payments and documents agree?

Record sales and delivery and payments and discrepancies according to the delivery slips and this enterprise's systems and complete settlement reconciliation and vehicle and equipment maintenance; records should agree with orders and payment documents to facilitate verification and handover; discrepancies and damage and returns and rejections are handled per the systems with records kept.

At accidents, stop, rescue, report, or leave the scene according to the actual personal injury/property damage situation under Article 70 of the traffic law; complaints/payment/equipment/food anomalies are handled under their respective applicable procedures, and can they be verified promptly and handed over? This table compares 'driver/sales workers' row by row with six adjacent positions that are easily confused within the same vehicle and delivery and sales content or have rotation and transfer relationships, by core work and outputs, key differences, and selection basis. The purpose of the comparison is not to rank them but to explain their respective duty boundaries and authorization scopes — in particular, long-haul transport authority, store pricing authority, cashier supervisor authority, and food safety and compliance conclusions cannot be assumed by this occupation as well.

The comparison should rest on three things: first, the work object (trunk goods and trailers, delivery items and routes, express items and waybills, store goods and customers, checkout counter and payment, inventory and locations); second, the basis and authorization (the respective application of delivery slips and route and price and payment rules and traffic and food safety requirements, freight transport procedures, delivery procedures, express service specifications, retail operating specifications, cashier procedures, and warehousing and order filling procedures); third, outputs and responsibility (who is responsible for completing route delivery and sales and payment collection and records on time, who is responsible for long-haul transport, who is responsible for pure delivery, who is responsible for pickup and delivery item timeliness, who is responsible for in-store closing, who is responsible for settlement, and who is responsible for stocking and order filling). When the three are inconsistent, the actual duties of the position and the traffic and practitioner qualification and food safety and payment system documents prevail.

The selection basis can follow three lines: if you want to drive along a set route and sell and collect payment while delivering, this page's occupation is the closest fit; if you want pure transport or pure delivery or pure pickup and delivery of items, heavy and tractor-trailer truck driver or light truck driver or courier and messenger are adjacent paths; if you want in-store closing or settlement or stocking and order filling, retail salesperson or cashier or stocker and order filler are another path. When transferring positions, what needs to be filled in is object knowledge and driving and practitioner qualifications and food safety and payment and store operating systems, not just proficiency.

Heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers (53-3032.00)

Drive heavy or tractor-trailer vehicles to complete long-haul and trunk freight, responsible for driving and vehicle and cargo safety and delivery and documents, and responsible for transport contracts and timeliness.

The object and duties differ: heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers focus on trunk goods and trailers and long-haul driving and usually do not take on sales and payment collection and stocking and display; this page's occupation focuses on route delivery and sales and payment collection and stocking, with smaller vehicles and routes but including sales and settlement duties. The basis and outputs differ and cannot be interchanged by name.

If you want to do long-haul and trunk freight, you can choose the heavy and tractor-trailer truck driver direction and check the driving and practitioner qualification requirements; if you want to deliver and sell along a route, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Light truck drivers (53-3033.00)

Drive light trucks to complete point-to-point or regional delivery, responsible for on-time delivery and sign-off and vehicle safety, and usually do not take on sales and payment collection and stocking duties.

The scope of duties differs: light truck drivers focus on pure delivery; in addition to delivery, this page's occupation also takes on order taking and introducing products and price changes and payment collection and stocking and promotional display and settlement. The difference in payment and sales systems from pure delivery means the tasks and outputs cannot be interchanged.
If you want to do pure delivery, you can choose the light truck driver direction; if you want to take on sales and payment collection in addition to delivery, this page's occupation is more suitable.
Couriers and messengers (43-5021.00)

The object and timeliness differ: couriers and messengers focus on pickup and delivery of items and express items and waybills and timeliness and work under express service specifications, and usually do not take on goods sales and payment settlement; this page's occupation focuses on goods and payments and customers and route sales, with different tasks and assessment.

If you want to do pickup and delivery work oriented to items and timeliness, you can choose the courier and messenger direction; if you want to do route delivery and sales and payment collection, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Retail salespersons (41-2031.00)

The scenario and authorization differ: retail salespersons receive customers and recommend and close sales in stores under retail operating and store pricing systems; this page's occupation completes delivery and sales and payment collection at the vehicle and customer site and does not take on store display management and inventory decision duties.
If you want to do in-store retail closing, you can choose the retail salesperson direction; if you want to run routes and close sales at customer sites, this page's occupation is more suitable.
Cashiers (41-2011.00)

The duties and authorization differ: cashiers scan, collect payment, give change, and reconcile at the checkout counter under cashier procedures and usually do not take on driving and delivery and stocking; this page's occupation collects payment and invoices and charges to accounts during delivery and takes on payment and document settlement, with a different payment scenario and scope of responsibility.
If you want to do cashiering and settlement, you can choose the cashier direction; if you want to combine driving and delivery with payment collection, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Stockers and Order Fillers (53-7065.00)

The scenario and content differ: stockers and order fillers organize and pick and verify goods in warehouses and stores under warehousing and order filling procedures; this page's occupation completes delivery and stocking and promotional display on routes and at customer sites, and organizing and picking goods is only part of it and must be combined with driving and payment collection.

If you want to do warehouse and store stocking and order filling, you can choose the stocker and order filler direction; if you want to run routes to complete delivery and sales, this page's occupation is more suitable.

The Provisions on the Administration of Road Transport Practitioners, Order No. 4 of 2026, fourth amendment, effective 2026-03-20, lists in Articles 2/6 the qualification subjects such as commercial passenger and freight drivers and dangerous goods; Article 10 covers the corresponding driving license for commercial freight, an age not exceeding 63, and related knowledge/examination certification, and it is not the case that all motor vehicle licenses are uniformly capped at 63. Article 29 provides that the qualification certificate is valid for 6 years and renewal is required no later than 30 days before expiry, and Article 32 provides for cancellation for exceeding 63 and other reasons. Article 38 applies to drivers and prohibits overloading and oversize loads, continuous driving of more than 4 hours, speeding, and fatigue; Article 46 sets 200—2000 yuan for missing, invalid, forged or altered, or out-of-scope passenger transport certificates and 200 yuan for freight under the same circumstances, with dangerous goods covered separately by Article 47 at 5—10 ten thousand yuan, and penalties are not mechanically applied as for ordinary freight. Article 52 provides that drivers of ordinary freight vehicles with a total mass of 4500 kg or less are not subject to these Provisions, which is not equivalent to exemption from the motor vehicle driving license, dangerous goods, or food obligations. Non-commercial activities cannot be said on this basis to be exempt from all qualifications, and taxis are subject to special rules that were not exhaustively verified this round, so it is not claimed that they are entirely unaffected.

Road Transport Regulations, sixth revision of 2026-01-30: Article 2 covers the scope of transport operations and related business; Articles 21/22 cover freight vehicles and safety management and driving licenses, and the age and knowledge examination by the competent authority (with an exception for ordinary freight of 4500 kg or less); Article 24 provides that ordinary freight operations of the same kind do not need the business license and vehicle operating certificate under that Article, which are business and vehicle formalities and not an individual driving permit. Article 28 applies to operator education and practitioner procedures and continuous driving of no more than 4 hours, and Articles 30/31 cover vehicle maintenance and inspection and the operator's emergency plan for accidents and the like. The actual nature of the operation, total mass, and cargo category must be verified and cannot be determined by the name driver/sales.

Road Traffic Safety Law 2021: Article 19 requires the corresponding driving license and permitted vehicle type; Article 21 requires a careful inspection of safety and technical performance before departure and prohibits driving a vehicle with safety hazards; Article 22 prohibits driving under conditions such as excessive fatigue that affect safe driving. Article 70 requires stopping immediately at an accident to protect the scene, immediately rescuing the injured and promptly calling the police; where there is no injury and no dispute over the facts and cause, the parties may immediately leave the scene and restore traffic and negotiate, and if they do not leave they must promptly call the police, while for minor property damage with clear facts they should leave first and then negotiate. Article 73 provides that the public security traffic management department prepares the accident determination letter, and the individual or organization does not issue a formal liability conclusion on its own. General complaints and payment discrepancies and accidents cannot be handled by the same stop-work and reporting sequence; enterprise restart systems were not obtained.

Food Safety Law 2025 revision government text: Article 33, item 6, covers safe, harmless, and clean containers, tools, and equipment for transport, storage, and loading and unloading, pollution prevention, the required temperature and humidity conditions, and not transporting together with toxic or harmful items; this item also applies to non-food operators engaged in storage, transport, and loading and unloading. Article 45 covers the health system and the annual health examination certificate for personnel who come into contact with directly edible food, and it is not a uniform health certificate for all packaged food delivery workers. Article 44 covers training and management of operating enterprises and the responsibility of the principal person in charge; Article 47 provides that if operating conditions no longer meet requirements rectification is required, and that if there is a potential food accident risk food operations must be stopped immediately and reported to the food safety department at or above the county level where the business is located; Article 63 provides that food that does not meet standards or may be harmful is stopped, notified, and recalled according to law by the corresponding producer or operator, and it is not an authority for delivery workers to destroy it at will. Article 41 additionally provides for a permitted transport system for road bulk transport of key liquid foods, which covers only that specific scope, and the specific catalog and supporting rules were not verified this round and are not generalized to ordinary parcels.

details: The Provisions on the Administration of Road Transport Practitioners, Order No. 4 of 2026, fourth amendment, effective 2026-03-20, lists in Articles 2/6 the qualification subjects such as commercial passenger and freight drivers and dangerous goods; Article 10 covers the corresponding driving license for commercial freight, an age not exceeding 63, and related knowledge/examination certification, and it is not the case that all motor vehicle licenses are uniformly capped at 63. Article 38 applies to drivers and prohibits overloading and oversize loads, continuous driving of more than 4 hours, speeding, and fatigue; Article 46 sets 200—2000 yuan for missing, invalid, forged or altered, or out-of-scope passenger transport certificates and 200 yuan for freight under the same circumstances, with dangerous goods covered separately by Article 47 at 5—10 ten thousand yuan, and penalties are not mechanically applied as for ordinary freight. Article 52 provides that drivers of ordinary freight vehicles with a total mass of 4500 kg or less are not subject to these Provisions, which is not equivalent to exemption from the motor vehicle driving license, dangerous goods, or food obligations. details: The Provisions on the Administration of Road Transport Practitioners, Order No. 4 of 2026, fourth amendment, effective 2026-03-20, lists in Articles 2/6 the qualification subjects such as commercial passenger and freight drivers and dangerous goods; Article 10 covers the corresponding driving license for commercial freight, an age not exceeding 63, and related knowledge/examination certification, and it is not the case that all motor vehicle licenses are uniformly capped at 63. Article 29 provides that the qualification certificate is valid for 6 years and renewal is required no later than 30 days before expiry, and Article 32 provides for cancellation for exceeding 63 and other reasons. Article 38 applies to drivers and prohibits overloading and oversize loads, continuous driving of more than 4 hours, speeding, and fatigue; Article 46 sets 200—2000 yuan for missing, invalid, forged or altered, or out-of-scope passenger transport certificates and 200 yuan for freight under the same circumstances, with dangerous goods covered separately by Article 47 at 5—10 ten thousand yuan, and penalties are not mechanically applied as for ordinary freight. Article 52 provides that drivers of ordinary freight vehicles with a total mass of 4500 kg or less are not subject to these Provisions, which is not equivalent to exemption from the motor vehicle driving license, dangerous goods, or food obligations. details: Road Traffic Safety Law 2021: Article 19 requires the corresponding driving license and permitted vehicle type; Article 21 requires a careful inspection of safety and technical performance before departure and prohibits driving a vehicle with safety hazards; Article 22 prohibits driving under conditions such as excessive fatigue that affect safe driving. Article 70 requires stopping immediately at an accident to protect the scene, immediately rescuing the injured and promptly calling the police; where there is no injury and no dispute over the facts and cause, the parties may immediately leave the scene and restore traffic and negotiate, and if they do not leave they must promptly call the police, while for minor property damage with clear facts they should leave first and then negotiate. Article 73 provides that the public security traffic management department prepares the accident determination letter, and the individual or organization does not issue a formal liability conclusion on its own. General complaints and payment discrepancies and accidents cannot be handled by the same stop-work and reporting sequence; enterprise restart systems were not obtained.

outlook_evidence.metric: Training and driving and practitioner qualification paths
outlook_evidence.value: The O*NET education feedback is only qualitative: some new hires require high school or equivalent and some less than high school; no percentages are invented. Job Zone1—2/SVP<6 is a preparation group with several days to one year of on-the-job training and does not mean the same course for every position. The BLS typical entry for this occupation is high school or equivalent, related experience None, and short-term on-the-job training; the OOH combined occupation narrative mentions 1 month or less of training and the requirement of a work-state driver's license and a good driving record, and the specific state/vehicle type conditions were not verified one by one. None does not mean training is unnecessary, and a lookup entry cannot prove nationwide exemption from driving licensing. The Provisions on the Administration of Road Transport Practitioners, Order No. 4 of 2026, fourth amendment, effective 2026-03-20, lists in Articles 2/6 the qualification subjects such as commercial passenger and freight drivers and dangerous goods; Article 10 covers the corresponding driving license for commercial freight, an age not exceeding 63, and related knowledge/examination certification, and it is not the case that all motor vehicle licenses are uniformly capped at 63. Article 29 provides that the qualification certificate is valid for 6 years and is renewed within 30 days before expiry, and Article 32 provides for cancellation for exceeding 63 and other reasons. Article 38 applies to drivers and prohibits overloading and oversize loads, continuous driving of more than 4 hours, speeding, and fatigue; Article 46 sets 200—2000 yuan for missing, invalid, forged or altered, or out-of-scope passenger transport certificates and 200 yuan for freight under the same circumstances, with dangerous goods covered separately by Article 47 at 5—10 ten thousand yuan, and penalties are not mechanically applied as for ordinary freight. Article 52 provides that drivers of ordinary freight vehicles with a total mass of 4500 kg or less are not subject to these Provisions, which is not equivalent to exemption from the motor vehicle driving license, dangerous goods, or food obligations. Non-commercial activities cannot be said on this basis to be exempt from all qualifications, and taxis are subject to special rules that were not exhaustively verified this round, so it is not claimed that they are entirely unaffected. Road Transport Regulations, sixth revision of 2026-01-30: Article 2 covers the scope of transport operations and related business; Articles 21/22 cover freight vehicles and safety management and driving licenses, and the age and knowledge examination by the competent authority (with an exception for ordinary freight of 4500 kg or less); Article 24 provides that ordinary freight operations of the same kind do not need the business license and vehicle operating certificate under that Article, which are business and vehicle formalities and not an individual driving permit. Article 28 applies to operator education and practitioner procedures and continuous driving of no more than 4 hours, and Articles 30/31 cover vehicle maintenance and inspection and the operator's emergency plan for accidents and the like. The actual nature of the operation, total mass, and cargo category must be verified and cannot be determined by the name driver/sales.

The Provisions on the Administration of Road Transport Practitioners, Order No. 4 of 2026, fourth amendment, effective 2026-03-20, lists in Articles 2/6 the qualification subjects such as commercial passenger and freight drivers and dangerous goods; Article 10 covers the corresponding driving license for commercial freight, an age not exceeding 63, and related knowledge/examination certification, and it is not the case that all motor vehicle licenses are uniformly capped at 63. Article 29 provides that the qualification certificate is valid for 6 years and renewal is required no later than 30 days before expiry, and Article 32 provides for cancellation for exceeding 63 and other reasons. Article 38 applies to drivers and prohibits overloading and oversize loads, continuous driving of more than 4 hours, speeding, and fatigue; Article 46 sets 200—2000 yuan for missing, invalid, forged or altered, or out-of-scope passenger transport certificates and 200 yuan for freight under the same circumstances, with dangerous goods covered separately by Article 47 at 5—10 ten thousand yuan, and penalties are not mechanically applied as for ordinary freight. Article 52 provides that drivers of ordinary freight vehicles with a total mass of 4500 kg or less are not subject to these Provisions, which is not equivalent to exemption from the motor vehicle driving license, dangerous goods, or food obligations. Non-commercial activities cannot be said on this basis to be exempt from all qualifications, and taxis are subject to special rules that were not exhaustively verified this round, so it is not claimed that they are entirely unaffected. Road Transport Regulations, sixth revision of 2026-01-30: Article 2 covers the scope of transport operations and related business; Articles 21/22 cover freight vehicles and safety management and driving licenses, and the age and knowledge examination by the competent authority (with an exception for ordinary freight of 4500 kg or less); Article 24 provides that ordinary freight operations of the same kind do not need the business license and vehicle operating certificate under that Article, which are business and vehicle formalities and not an individual driving permit. Article 28 applies to operator education and practitioner procedures and continuous driving of no more than 4 hours, and Articles 30/31 cover vehicle maintenance and inspection and the operator's emergency plan for accidents and the like. The actual nature of the operation, total mass, and cargo category must be verified and cannot be determined by the name driver/sales. Road Traffic Safety Law 2021: Article 19 requires the corresponding driving license and permitted vehicle type; Article 21 requires a careful inspection of safety and technical performance before departure and prohibits driving a vehicle with safety hazards; Article 22 prohibits driving under conditions such as excessive fatigue that affect safe driving. Article 70 requires stopping immediately at an accident to protect the scene, immediately rescuing the injured and promptly calling the police; where there is no injury and no dispute over the facts and cause, the parties may immediately leave the scene and restore traffic and negotiate, and if they do not leave they must promptly call the police, while for minor property damage with clear facts they should leave first and then negotiate. Article 73 provides that the public security traffic management department prepares the accident determination letter, and the individual or organization does not issue a formal liability conclusion on its own. General complaints and payment discrepancies and accidents cannot be handled by the same stop-work and reporting sequence; enterprise restart systems were not obtained. Food Safety Law 2025 revision government text: Article 33, item 6, covers safe, harmless, and clean containers, tools, and equipment for transport, storage, and loading and unloading, pollution prevention, the required temperature and humidity conditions, and not transporting together with toxic or harmful items; this item also applies to non-food operators engaged in storage, transport, and loading and unloading. subject.summary: Driver/sales workers (U.S. side O*NET-SOC 53-3031.00, Driver/Sales Workers) are route sales positions that drive a vehicle along a set route or within a set area to sell and collect payment while delivering: they drive a truck or other vehicle to sell or deliver goods such as food and restaurant takeout, or to collect and deliver items such as commercial laundry; the work includes verifying the delivery slips and orders and route and loading goods, inspecting the vehicle and food dispensing equipment, driving along the route and delivering and obtaining sign-off at the delivery point, introducing new products and price changes and taking orders, stocking shelves and setting up promotional displays or handing out promotional materials, collecting payment and restocking and removing stale goods for vending machines, collecting payment and giving change and issuing receipts or charging to the account per the order, handling customer complaints about goods or services, recording sales and delivery information on the daily sales or delivery record, completing payment and document settlement and reconciliation and handling discrepancies and returns and rejections, maintaining the vehicle and food dispensing equipment and cleaning the interior of food or beverage dispensers, and reporting and handing over as required when damage or complaints or accidents or equipment anomalies occur. U.S. definition: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 38,770 USD per year (18.64 USD per hour), with annual percentiles of 22,590 / 30,200 / 38,770 / 49,000 / 59,980 USD (hourly percentiles 10.86 / 14.52 / 18.64 / 23.56 / 28.84); the O*NET summary page gives 2024 employment of about 451,500, a 2024—2034 projection of 'much faster than average (Much faster than average, 7% or higher)', and about 51,300 projected job openings (that source gives only the category and threshold rather than a single precise percentage, and this page follows the source wording); the preparation level is Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), the education feedback this round is only a qualitative answer (some positions require a high school diploma or equivalent and some require less than high school), the interest code is RCE, and there are 11 tasks; the work context includes outdoor exposure to all kinds of weather 'every day' 100%, time pressure every day 92%, exposure to extreme heat or extreme cold every day 82%, repeating the same tasks 'extremely important' 76%, continuous use of hands 76%, inside an enclosed vehicle every day 78%, face-to-face discussions every day 77%, decision freedom 'very large' 43%, decisions every day 39%, having to deal with unpleasant or angry people every day 19%, conflict situations 'weekly or more' 26%, work hours 'regular' 82%, continuous repetitive motions 64%, continuous bending or twisting 59%, exposure to contaminants every day 40%, competition 'extremely competitive' 21%, consequences of error 'extremely serious' 32%, and working more than 40 hours per week 81%. Mainland China definition: drivers engaged in commercial road passenger and freight transport must obtain the corresponding practitioner qualification certificate under the Provisions on the Administration of Road Transport Practitioners (Ministry of Transport Order No. 4 of 2026, fourth amendment, published February 6, 2026 and effective from March 20, 2026); failing to obtain the corresponding practitioner qualification certificate, or using an invalid, forged, or altered certificate, or driving a road passenger vehicle beyond the approved scope is ordered to be corrected and fined not less than 200 yuan and not more than 2000 yuan, and driving a road freight vehicle in the same circumstances is ordered to be corrected and fined 200 yuan (Article forty-six); drivers using ordinary freight vehicles with a total mass of 4500 kg or less and drivers of non-commercial private vehicles do not need to obtain the practitioner qualification certificate, and these Provisions do not cover taxi drivers; at the same time the Road Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China and (where food delivery is involved) the Food Safety Law of the People's Republic of China and the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests must be observed. The above is cited by regulation name and general requirements, and article numbers were not verified one by one. This occupation has no unified access-type occupational qualification in mainland China. Public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage definition corresponding to this occupation, this page preserves the gap as it stands, and industry average wages serve only as a visible industry proxy.
